The L1–L4 admission gate operates as a sequential filter enforcing semantic fidelity. L1 ensures minimal textual detail, L2 validates physical grounding, L3 checks logical consistency of offsets, and L4 confirms semantic entailment. Each layer introduces a binary predicate that partitions the corpus into admitted and rejected subsets. Failures in any layer lead to rejection, with L2 and L4 being particularly sensitive to misalignment between quoted content and source document structure. The audit reveals systemic flaws in L3 and L4 logic, such as incorrect handling of missing quotes and flawed entailment checks, which inflate false positives and undermine trust in the admission process. These failures expose a dual nature of the gate: it can be both a validator and a generator of spurious results depending on implementation fidelity.
